title: Kasper Schmeichel out of World Cup with ‘devastating’ injury: ‘It could be the end of my career’
content:
Kasper Schmeichel revealed on Tuesday that he will under two surgeries on his shoulder and fears that he has played “his last ever football game”.

The goalkeeper had previously ruled himself out of contention for Denmark’s upcoming World Cup play-offs with the issue that he said to Danish broadcaster TV2 stems from playing with a broken shoulder last year.

Schmeichel, 39, has been Celtic’s no 1 but has not played since February 22 after also suffering with illness, and his contract expires at the end of the season.

He appeared on the Champions League after-show on Tuesday, having attended Manchester City’s 2-1 defeat to Real Madrid, and said he “might not be able” to play again.

“I was at a specialist yesterday and they told me I need two surgeries to fix my shoulder,” Schmeichel said on CBS/Paramount+ coverage, with his father Peter Schmeichel and former City defender Micah Richards who are pundits.

“It’s a bit of a body blow. There’s issues with my bicep and my rotator cuff. Everything has gone. It’s a bit like an outfield doing their ACL (anterior cruciate ligament) and their Achilles at the same time.

“There will be at least 10 to 12 months of rehab. I don’t really know anything right now. I don’t know how to react. I could potentially have played my last ever football game. I have been a footballer since the day I was born. It is devastating. To think I might not be able to do that again is tough. I got the message yesterday that it could be the end of my career.

“I’m going to fight and do my rehab. The first surgery is next Friday and then the big surgery will follow.”

Schmeichel has kept 12 clean sheets in 26 league matches this term and played all of Denmark’s World Cup qualifiers this year, captaining the side against Greece in October. Celtic head coach Martin O’Neill confirmed in a press conference on March 6 he had taken an injection and returned to training but the Dane told TV2 this month he had taken a “bad turn”.

“A year ago I broke my shoulder against Portugal, but stayed on the field and played on because we didn’t have any more substitutions,” he said. “It has caused a lot of after-effects that have been hard to live with — and play with.

“But the last few months things have taken a bad turn with my shoulder, and it has really caused problems for me.”

Schmeichel has made 120 senior international appearances. After coming through Manchester City’s academy he spent 11 years at Leicester City, where he won the Premier League in the 2015-16 season.
